findings.title: Spawn/villager removal reports success even when the arenas.yml write failed
findings.problem: removeSpawnPoint() discards the boolean returned by saveSpawnPoints() and always returns true. removeMobSpawnPoint() (line 692) and removeVillager() (line 728) have the identical shape. The published contract in ArenaAdminService#deleteSpawnPoint says "true = deleted; ... false on write failure", and the class itself tracks failures through saveSpawnPoints()/lastSaveFailed, so the GUI path loses the only failure signal it has.
findings.impact: When arenas.yml is in read-only degradation (quarantined/parse failure) or the atomic write throws IOException, the admin management GUI shows "manage.entry.deleted" for a point that is still on disk. The in-memory list no longer contains it, so the GUI list also appears shorter for the rest of the session; after a restart the deleted spawn point / villager comes back, and villagers silently reappear on a map the admin believes was edited. For spawn points the next game can teleport players to a point the admin tried to delete.
findings.trigger: ArenaManageGUI -> right-click a spawn/mob-spawn/villager entry -> ArenaAdminService#deleteSpawnPoint/deleteMobSpawnPoint/deleteVillager -> AdminDeployManager#remove*, while arenas.yml writes are blocked or fail (gate read-only, IO error, full disk).

findings.title: Arena reset is allowed during the VICTORY/DEFEAT settlement countdown and kicks players mid-settlement
findings.problem: canReset() gates only STARTING/RUNNING/WAVE_INTERMISSION and ENDING. GameState.VICTORY and GameState.DEFEAT - the settlement countdown, during which players are still inside the arena - fall through to Gate.OK. MultiArenaManager#disableArena() likewise rejects only the three in-play states, so the reset proceeds: disableArena -> stopGame() evicts every player and the map is cleared/rolled back while the victory/defeat summary is still running. The sibling admin operation explicitly treats those states as in-progress (ArenaAdminService#updateGameParams returns COUNTDOWN_IN_PROGRESS for VICTORY/DEFEAT), and NpcManager#isGameInProgress also counts VICTORY/DEFEAT as "players still on the field"; only this destructive path ignores them.
findings.impact: Players are teleported out and their session is destroyed before the settlement finishes (stat summary and scoreboard state are cut off), and the shop NPC is despawned underneath them, even though the same GUI refuses to merely edit min-players in that window. The arena then proceeds straight to a map rollback while the defeat/victory broadcast is still in flight.
findings.trigger: /hilltop manage -> arena detail -> reset -> confirm while the arena's GameState is VICTORY or DEFEAT (defeat/victory countdown ticking, players still inside).

findings.title: Reset despawns the shop NPC before deployment-data clearing; a failed clear leaves the re-enabled arena with no shop
findings.problem: Step 7 irreversibly removes the physical shop villager (NpcManager#despawnIfInWorld -> despawnNpc) before step 8 calls ArenaManager#clearDeploymentData(). If step 8 fails, abort() rolls back nodes.yml and then calls reinstate(), which re-enables the arena - but nothing re-spawns the shop NPC and arenas.yml still contains arenas.<id>.shop-npc. The rollback therefore restores "enabled" but not the state that step 7 destroyed, and no marker records that the NPC was removed.
findings.impact: After an aborted reset (arenas.yml write failure, e.g. read-only degradation or IO error) the arena is playable again but the plugin-level shop NPC is gone: right-clicking the shop no longer opens the shop for anyone, even though the GUI still reports the arena as having a shop and /hilltop deploy listshows a shop-npc position. It only comes back after a full server restart (NpcManager#respawnFromConfig).
findings.trigger: Reset an arena that has a shop NPC, with arenas.yml write failing at clearDeploymentData (read-only gate or IOException) - proceed() aborts at step 8 after step 7 already despawned the entity.

findings.title: Core coordinates are read without an isSet guard, so a damaged core node becomes core (x, y, 0) and is later persisted
findings.problem: The core node is read with ConfigurationSection#getDouble and no isSet/finite check. Bukkit returns 0.0 for a missing key, so a core section that lost one coordinate (hand edit, truncated write, or a file written by an older schema) is accepted as a valid core at that 0 coordinate instead of being treated as undeployed. The same class does guard the other nodes it reads (readLocation() at line 420 uses isSet and Double.isFinite and returns null), and ArenaManager#readOptionalLocation() would also have rejected the damaged core; only this reader manufactures a value.
findings.impact: Any subsequent deployment action on this arena (addspawn, setcore of another field, setshop, removeVillager...) calls saveSpawnPoints(), which writes the invented core back to arenas.yml (line 514-516) and pushes it to gameManager. The core then genuinely is at coordinate 0 on that axis: the arena counts as deployed (hasCore true, enableArena allowed), players respawn/teleport to the world origin area (possibly void or another map region), and the admin never sees a warning about the damaged node because only the ArenaManager reader is defensive.
findings.trigger: Hand-edited/partially damaged arenas.yml with a core section missing x, y or z (e.g. core: {x: 100, y: 70}), then any AdminDeployManager operation that saves (or a shop-NPC migration) while the world is loaded.

findings.title: One malformed spawn-point entry drops the whole arena from the registry instead of skipping the point
findings.problem: readDefinition() only tolerates list entries that are not Maps (they are skipped with a warning at line 572-575), but for a Map entry readLocationFromMap() throws IllegalArgumentException when x/y/z is missing or non-finite (mapDouble, line 653-659), and that exception is not caught locally. It escapes to load()'s per-arena catch (line 188-191), which drops the entire definition - no registry entry at all. The same defensiveness used for core/shop-npc/waiting-location (readOptionalLocation) and the explicit warning for non-map entries are bypassed by one bad coordinate.
findings.impact: A single corrupted spawn point (or a .NaN value, which mapDouble rejects) makes the arena disappear from /hilltop list, the selection GUI and the management GUI. ArenaResetService then answers ARENA_NOT_FOUND, so the admin cannot reset the arena to recover it from inside the game, and cannot even see which arena is broken without reading the console log. Mob spawn points have the identical failure mode (line 592).
findings.trigger: /hilltop reloadconfig or startup load with arenas.<id>.spawn-points containing a map entry that lacks x/y/z or holds NaN/Infinity.

findings.title: Failed arenas.yml write still replaces the live arena's spawn points and core in memory
findings.problem: The in-memory push to GameManager runs unconditionally after `boolean saved = gate.write(arenasConfig);`; the write result is only stored in lastSaveFailed. On failure the disk still holds the old deployment data while the running arena immediately uses the new spawn points, mob spawn points and core. There is no rollback and no reload, so the process state and arenas.yml diverge until restart.
findings.impact: A deployment command whose save failed is reported as failed (reportDeploySaveFailure), yet the live arena already switched: players respawn/teleport to points that exist only in memory, and the next successful save of any arena field writes those unsaved points to disk after all. Admins who see the failure message and re-edit the YAML on disk are silently overridden in the running server.
findings.trigger: Any deployment edit (addspawn, setcore, setwaiting, removeVillager...) while arenas.yml is read-only or the atomic write fails; saveSpawnPoints continues past the failed gate.write.

unverified: No build or test execution was performed; all findings are static call-graph reasoning over the 11 assigned files plus the directly implicated callee snippets (MultiArenaManager#disableArena/enableArena, NpcManager#despawnIfInWorld/isGameInProgress, GameManager#setSpawnPoints/setCoreLocation, NodeSystem static node IO, YamlFiles/YamlFileGate).

ArenaDefinition has no world/region bounding-box or min/max corner fields in this revision (only optional core/shopNpc/waitingLocation plus point lists and scalar radii), so the 'inverted region bounds' hypothesis could not be mapped to any code and was not reported.

ArenaManageGUI/AbstractAdminMenu click and drag guards were read in full and no bypass was found: guardClick cancels every click whose top-inventory holder is the menu instance, guardDrag cancels when any raw slot falls inside the top inventory, and the parent dispatcher additionally re-checks the clicked inventory. The suspected GUI-guard defect is therefore not reported.

LocationParticlePreview was checked for leaked tasks: the map is keyed per player UUID, a new show() cancels the previous task, tasks self-cancel when the viewer is offline or the duration elapses, and onDisable calls stopAll(); no concrete leak was quoted.

YamlFiles.write was verified to use a unique temp name + ATOMIC_MOVE, so the 'half-written arenas.yml' scenario is mitigated at the file level; the residual multi-write (spawn data then shop-npc as two separate atomic writes) is noted only as context, not reported as its own finding.
notes: Slice S05 read in full (11/11 files). Six findings kept; the strongest are the GUI deletion path that reports success on a failed save (S05-F1) and the reset path that despawns the shop NPC before the step that can fail (S05-F3). Deleting one spawn point is enough to lose the whole arena definition (S05-F5), and the deploy reader manufactures a 0-coordinate core from a damaged node (S05-F4), which then gets persisted. All evidence strings were re-read from the cited line ranges after writing and contain only ASCII source text; no comment-only lines are used as evidence.
